text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: metrics_pipeline.scrape_errors (high)
pagerduty: Incident PD-29571 created -> https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-29571 Urgency: high. Trigger: prom-scrape-job 'prod/prometheus-scrape' failing > 5m
alex: acked on pagerduty, I'm oncall now. pulling up dashboards :eyes:
maria: seeing scrape errors + a growing log-ingest backlog in kafka-consumer-lag metric. possible backpressure from log pipeline.
jyoti: can you post the top error? short logs help.
alex: here's the latest from prom-collector logs (last 3 lines):
```
2026-03-14T10:02:11Z ERROR scrape: target="infra/node-exporter" err="context deadline exceeded"
2026-03-14T10:02:12Z WARN  queue: processing delay=1850ms partitions_unbalanced=1
2026-03-14T10:02:13Z ERROR kafka-consumer: lag=124000 group=log-ingest topic=logs-ingest
```
alex: PromQL queries show spike in `scrape_timeout_count` starting ~10:00 UTC and kafka consumer lag >100k for logs-ingest group.
maria: customer impact? any dashboards missing for external customers?
jyoti: yes, a handful of customers report missing dashboard metrics and delayed logs in SIEM. Severity: partial data-loss (near-real-time missing).
darren: tagging eng-runtime and eng-infra incase this is infra-level. @eng-runtime @eng-infra
alex: quick actions I ran: checked prometheus targets -> many targets in UNKNOWN. Tried restarting prom-collector pod in eu-west-1 staging-router: `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment/prom-collector` — didn't fully recover, errors persisted.
alex: trying to scale log-consumer group to reduce backlog
```
# scale kafka consumers in prod
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/log-consumer --replicas=6
```
maria: scaling seems to reduce lag for one partition, but partitions_unbalanced persists. Kafka cluster shows an ISR rebalance event around 09:58 UTC.
jyoti: could be a broker-level network jitter causing both scrape timeouts (targets behind VPC peering) and kafka rebalances.
oncall-sre: also seeing an AWS EBS io-wait spike on brokers in eu-west-1 between 09:56-10:04 (cloudwatch link: https://aws.console/.../metrics).
darren: runbook for metrics-pipeline -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/metrics-pipeline. Follow step 2 (check brokers, remap partitions) and step 5 (fallback to cached metrics in resizing service).
alex: mapping plan: 1) temporarily increase prom scrape_timeout from 10s to 20s for noisy jobs 2) rebalance kafka partitions by triggering preferred leader election for offline partitions 3) enable scraping fallback cache for critical customers
jyoti: do we have permission for preferred leader election now? that can be noisy.
maria: I'm ok with doing it if we coordinate and monitor for further rebalances. we need to communicate to stakeholders first.
alex: I'll execute preferred leader election on affected brokers now. will watch consumer lag.
(alex executes command)
```
kafka-preferred-leader-election.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-prod:9092 --topic logs-ingest --verbose
```
alex: started election, monitoring...
pagerduty: PD-29571: acknowledged by alex at 2026-03-14T10:07:05Z
jyoti: after election, ISR stabilised and consumer lag dropped to ~12k. scrape timeouts reduced but not gone.
maria: next mitigation: bump prom scrape timeout for target groups behind the VPC peering to 20s, apply as temp config.
alex: applied config patch to prometheus `prometheus-main` config map, reloaded config via `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart statefulset/prometheus-main`.
(alex posts diff)
```
- scrape_config: job_name: 'vpc-targets' scrape_timeout: '10s'
+ scrape_config: job_name: 'vpc-targets' scrape_timeout: '20s' # temporary
```
jyoti: after reload, scrape success rate increased from 68% -> 92% over next 4 mins.
darren: customer impact update: core dashboards regained data for most customers; a subset still missing due to KV cache warmup.
oncall-sre: opening a follow-up ticket to track long-term fixes: PROD-8472 (kafka broker storage performance + prom scrape resilience)
maria: handoff plan: alex is staying for mitigation and verifying, then i'll take follow-up overnight check. if anything spikes, page again.
alex: current status: PD-29571 -> acknowledged, mitigations applied (kafka preferred-leader, scaled consumers, increased scrape_timeout), partial recovery observed. monitoring for 30m before close.
pagerduty: PD-29571 -> note added: "mitigations applied, partial recovery; monitoring" by alex
jyoti: suggest we add automated detection for ISR rebalance correlated to prom scrape failures to avoid manual ops next time.
darren: agreed, filing a post-incident action item.
(incident-bot): Reminder: please fill incident template -> https://redwood.internal/incidents/new with timeline and customer impact
alex: leaving a short timeline in the incident doc and will handoff to maria at 11:00 UTC. tagging @maria for takeover.
maria: taking over at 11:00 UTC. thanks all. :thumbsup:
